meetings.title: Juniper Foods: intro call
segments: Hi Hiro, can you hear me okay?
Yes, perfectly. Sorry, I'm in a coffee shop, there might be some background noise.
No problem at all. Thanks for making time.
Hiro, thanks for reaching out after the webinar.
What made you get in touch?
So, Juniper is a meal kit company, about a hundred and fifty people.
We get a lot of feedback, mostly through app reviews and our support inbox.
When something goes wrong, like a bad batch of an ingredient, reviews spike and we find out a few days too late.
How often does something like that happen?
A few times a quarter.
Last month it was a supplier change that made one of our sauces taste different.
We got two hundred reviews about it in a week.
Our rating dropped from four point six to four point two.
Ouch. That's a big drop for a week.
It took about a month to recover.
And app store rating directly affects how many new customers we get.
How did you eventually find the cause?
A customer tagged us on social media with a photo of the ingredient label.
That's how we found out about the supplier change.
Not a great way to find out.
How do you find out today?
Usually someone on the team notices the app rating dropping.
By then it's already in the reviews, publicly, which is the worst place for it.
What happens once you spot something?
That's the second problem. If it's a bug in the app, I have to write it up and put it in Jira for the product team.
It's manual, and half the time the context gets lost.
Being able to send a theme straight to Jira would save me a lot of time.
Who else on your team would use the product?
My two support leads, and probably our head of product.
She's the one who'd really benefit from seeing what customers are saying without waiting for me to summarize it.
That's a great use case.
Product teams are often the biggest fans.
That's a common request. I'll be transparent, a full two-way Jira integration isn't available yet.
A simpler way to create a Jira issue from a theme is something the team is actively discussing.
What does the handoff to product look like today, step by step?
I copy a few reviews into a Jira ticket, write a summary, and guess at the priority.
Then product asks me how many people are affected, and I go back and count by hand.
It usually takes three or four back and forths.
So the count is the missing piece.
Exactly. If the ticket said 'two hundred reviews this week, growing', nobody would need to ask.
Even one way would be enough for me.
I don't need it to sync back.
That's really useful to hear.
Can I ask about budget?
We're a small team, so it's tight.
I'd guess ten to fifteen thousand a year at most.
I'd need to see pricing before I can take it to our COO.
Is there a particular time you'd want to have something in place?
Not urgent. Ideally before our spring menu launch, because that's when we change the most recipes and the most things can go wrong.
Understood. Let me send you our pricing sheet and a short recorded demo you can share with your COO.
Then let's do a proper follow-up discovery in a couple of weeks, once you've had a look.
One more question. If the Jira button comes out, would it be included in the plan, or extra?
I'd expect it to be included, but I'll confirm before I say it for sure.
I'll include that in my follow-up.
That works for me. Thanks, Aisha.
